The rain lashed against the floor-to-ceiling windows of the penthouse office, blurring the city lights into streaks of gold and neon. Inside, the air was sterile and cold, smelling faintly of expensive leather and anxiety.

Elena Vance sat behind her desk, a fortress of mahogany and silence. To the outside world, she was the epitome of corporate efficiency: the woman who remembered every coffee order, scheduled every merger, and never missed a deadline. But to Julian Thorne, the CEO of Aethelgard Dynamics, she was something else entirely. She was the only person who knew where he kept the unencrypted flash drive containing the "Project Chimera" data—the very project that had nearly bankrupted the company three years ago.

Julian paced the room, his tie loosened, his eyes bloodshot. He had just received a call from a rival firm. They knew. They knew about the data leak, and they knew it was coming from the inside.
